tenures.note: Billed from Toronto, Ontario, Canada, weighing 121 pounds, representing the Bod Squad; entered mimicking the look and old entrance of former friend Erin McCoys. Lost by pinfall (Burn Cycle) in a non-title women's contest, then ambushed McCoys after the match with a kick-start DDT and a double armscissors and legscissors hold. Teamed with Bliss as the Bod Squad on 22 October 2003, again entering in the same borrowed look and calling herself the "New Blonde Bombshell," in a win over Marissa Monet and Sierra Browne. Lost a non-title women's contest to Lolita Love on 17 December 2003, her own Ray of Sunshine submission hold reversed into a rollup for the pin. Married to Tom Landis; lost an intergender tag match with him on 24 March 2004 to Alex Kidd and Alicia Powers when Powers's own Somersault Bulldog assist set up the pinfall on Landis. Attacked Alicia Powers with Brianna Landis after Powers's own win on 25 August 2004, chased off by Tara Smith. Lost to Tara Smith by disqualification on 28 August 2004 after striking her with a tag team title belt in front of the referee, then continued the beatdown with Landis until Alicia Powers ran in. Retained the UWF Women's Tag Team Championship with tag partner Brianna Landis over Team BATTLE*DREAM by disqualification on 8 September 2004, driving a chair into Misaki Ishikawa's spine to save Landis from a spike piledriver. Lost a non-title six-woman tag alongside Brianna Landis and a late-arriving Donna Tetreault to Sierra Browne and Team BATTLE*DREAM on 2 October 2004, tased by Misaki Ishikawa mid-match; Sierra Browne's Truth Superkick finished Landis for the pin. Confronted Commissioner Becky Byers backstage on 27 November 2004 over a referee's own beating at the hands of the Bod Squad's challengers, only for Byers to announce a UWF Women's Tag Team Championship defense against Team BATTLE*DREAM ("Tornado" Tara Smith, Alicia Powers) at Rise to Power. Knocked out Misaki Ishikawa at ringside with the Bod Squad's own championship belt during Brianna Landis's own win over Reona Yoshida on 1 December 2004, then used Ishikawa's own taser on a bystander identified only as Rocko. Lost with tag partner Brianna Landis to "Tornado" Tara Smith and Alicia Powers by pinfall on 25 May 2005, telling Landis beforehand that she had "worked something out" with an unnamed man. Joined Brianna Landis in ambushing Lisa Drake from behind at John DeWolfe's direction on 8 June 2005, then broke up Alicia Powers and "Tornado" Tara Smith's own match against Drake and Leslie Hernandez, ending it as a no contest. Accompanied John DeWolfe and Brianna Landis to the ring on 22 June 2005 to belittle the women's division, backing DeWolfe's own praise of the Bod Squad before being run off by Lisa Drake, Alicia Powers, and "Tornado" Tara Smith. Lost to Alicia Powers by disqualification on 6 July 2005 after Brianna Landis interfered twice, having told husband Tom Landis beforehand that she meant to end Alicia's own wrestling career. Ran in with Bod Squad partner Brianna Landis during the Wind Walkers' own women's tag match on 20 July 2005, attacking Tara Smith before Lisa Drake, Arielle Starr, and Leslie Hernandez helped clear the ring. Teamed with Brianna Landis and John DeWolfe to beat Lisa Drake and the Wind Walkers by pinfall on 6 August 2005. Lost to Fantasy Girl by pinfall (a second-rope fisherman buster) on 7 June 2006, then was attacked further after the bell -- a top-rope double moonsault kneedrop, a Death Valley Driver off the ring apron, and a 450 splash onto her own stretcher -- when Fantasy Girl unmasked as her own sister-in-law, Brianna Landis.

tenures.note: Cornered for Fury and the One-Winged Angel in earlier Amity appearances before her own in-ring debut; teamed with Fury (Rage, Spice) to beat Team Canada (Trevor Hextall, Bob Jablonski) and Kari Stevens by pinfall in her own first competitive UWF match, finishing Stevens with a version of the One-Winged Angel's own Revelator. Needled Rage and Spice over Amity's own flat mood ahead of their own losing UWF World Tag Team Championship challenge to the Privateers on 1 December 2004. On 11 December 2004, cornered the One-Winged Angel through his own no-contest with "Dead End" Derek Martin, slapping Martin across the head and being shoved off the apron for it. Challenged new champion Sierra Browne to a future UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship match on 28 May 2005 over the Misfits' own objections, and had the challenge accepted. Beat Kari Stevens by submission (the Woman's Scorn) on 8 June 2005 with members of both Amity and Team Canada at ringside, drawing an approving Sierra Browne down to watch. Backed Rage of Fury at ringside for a Road to the Gold qualifier on 22 June 2005. Introduced "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict as Amity's own newest member on 28 April 2007, then joined her in accepting a future title challenge from Women's North American Champion Sonya Benedict, Myra's own cousin.

tenures.note: Fought Myra Benedict to a fifteen-minute time-limit draw in a number-one-contender's match, earning a three-way UWF Women's Championship shot against Stephanie Harper the following week. Attacked afterward by Tigress and Leslie Hernandez of Sabbat Justice's Coven. Wrestled that promised three-way title match on 25 October 2003 with open disinterest, making no attempt to prevent Stephanie Harper's pinfall over Myra Benedict. Teamed with Randall Osbourne on 20 December 2003 in a losing intergender tag match against Avanter and Angel; driven down twice by Osbourne's own tag partner Avanter with a full-nelson suplex and a full-nelson backbreaker, she began coughing up blood and the referee stopped the match after Angel applied the Altar of Fire. Taken to a local hospital for observation afterward. Ambushed backstage with a chair by "Twilight Angel" Sonya Benedict on 24 March 2004; beat Benedict by disqualification on 5 May 2004 after Benedict busted her open with a fluorescent light tube, saved by Tesla St. James and Lisa Drake. Teamed with Lisa Drake as Extreme Measures in a losing four corners women's tag war on 25 August 2004 against Melody and Comedy, the Love Sisters, and the debuting Team BATTLE*DREAM, continuing to brawl with Yoshida and Ishikawa after the bell. Teamed with Lisa Drake as Extreme Measures in a losing tag match against Alicia Powers and Tara Smith on 22 September 2004, pinned alongside Drake by Smith's own top-rope Arizona Rattler. Beat Leanna Love by pinfall (the Dragon Spike) in a lumberjill match on 20 October 2004, ending the pair's own long friendship-turned-rivalry. Talked a reluctant Alex Extreme into accepting her as a late substitute for the injured Lisa Drake, then lost alongside him to Kyle Lee and Tesla St. James by pinfall on 27 November 2004. Earlier saved Lisa Drake from a beating by Allison Ivey and Jacob Drake, clearing Ivey from the ring with a string of headbutts and helping carry Lisa out on a makeshift gurney. Told Moe Owens in a backstage interview on 28 May 2005 that she was refocusing on the singles ranks after a non-title win over Sierra Browne in Bangor, and revealed that her own feud with Sonya Benedict, including a real attack on herself, had been an elaborate scheme against Edmond Winston IV and Jessica Marshall. Caught up with Sonya Benedict backstage on 11 June 2005 over drinks, thanking her for the real chairshot she once took to help sell their shared scheme against Edmond Winston IV and Jessica Marshall. Beat "All Night" Wendy Minow by pinfall (a Dragon Spike kick) on 6 July 2005 in a return to singles competition, telling reporter Moe Owens beforehand that she meant to work her way back up the rankings rather than demand a title shot from Sierra Browne. Beat Donna Tetreault by pinfall (a Dragon Spike kick) in a Women's Heavyweight Championship number-one contenders match on 20 July 2005 after the referee restarted the bout on Stephanie Harper's own insistence, ruling Tetreault had used the ropes for leverage on an earlier rollup. Was interviewed by Moe Owens on 6 August 2005 and then attacked backstage by Serge Annis and Caliban of the Hands of Death, in retaliation for her brothers' own actions against the team.

tenures.note: Teamed with sister Lolita Love and Comedy against the Coven (Tigress, Leslie Hernandez, and Angel); pinned by Leslie Hernandez's top-rope Santa Maria. Billed with Lolita as the reigning UWF Women's Tag Team Champions, though the title itself was not on the line in this three-on-three match. Lost a non-title singles match to Lisa Drake by rollup on 15 November 2003 after Tara Marshall ran in from the crowd and knocked out cornerwoman Lolita Love with the ring steps. Teamed with sister Lolita Love as the Love Sisters in a losing four corners women's tag war on 25 August 2004 against Melody and Comedy, the debuting Team BATTLE*DREAM, and Extreme Measures. Lost to "Mockingbird" Nina Grimsson by pinfall (the Dragon Spike) in a lumberjill match on 20 October 2004, ending the pair's own long friendship-turned-rivalry. Was beaten down backstage by Moira Faith and Myra Benedict ahead of her own Women's Tag Team Championship challenge on 11 June 2005, refused medical treatment, and lost the title match anyway alongside sister Lolita. Confronted younger sister Lolita on 6 July 2005 over letting the Kindred escape with information on their kidnapped cat's captor, warning her against getting close to Moira Faith alone. Told Moe Owens that sister Lolita would be sidelined by the Kindred's own torture on 3 August 2005; fought Angel and the Kindred to a no-contest alongside Sonya Benedict on 6 August 2005, then captured and pistol-whipped Moira Faith with brass knuckles before sister Lolita talked her out of using a katana on her.

tenures.note: Teamed with sister Leanna Love and Comedy against the Coven; made the post-match save on Leanna after the bell. Billed with Leanna as the reigning UWF Women's Tag Team Champions. Beat Tara Marshall by pinfall in a non-title women's contest on 17 December 2003, reversing Marshall's own Ray of Sunshine submission hold into a rollup. Teamed with sister Leanna Love as the Love Sisters in a losing four corners women's tag war on 25 August 2004, pinned alongside Melody by Reona Yoshida's own double DDT. Lost to Leslie Hernandez by pinfall (a cradle) in a friendly Miss Uni rivalry match on 28 August 2004 after a prolonged assault on her own leg. Lost to Dalbello Rage by pinfall (a super cradleplex) on 22 September 2004 after a prolonged leg attack, despite pre-match scouting help from cousin Lara Leigh Love; suplexed over the top rope into sister Leanna's arms afterward. Tried to shield a bloodied Moira Faith in the Love Sisters' own locker room on 11 June 2005 before Faith and Myra Benedict turned on her and sister Leanna, then lost her own Women's Tag Team Championship challenge afterward, refusing medical treatment beforehand. Defended sparing Moira Faith and "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict to sister Leanna on 6 July 2005, hoping to reason with Faith over their own kidnapped cat, Mr. Boo Boo, through a mutual friend, Lara Leigh. Cornered Moira Faith alone in a bathroom backstage on 20 July 2005 to ask about her own kidnapped cat, Mr. Boo Boo, and was instead attacked and threatened by Moira, "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict, and Caine Tainer, who cut her forehead on broken glass from a shattered mirror. Shown bound and tortured by the Kindred in footage aired 3 August 2005, ruled out of that week's tag match as a result; on 6 August 2005 stopped sister Leanna from cutting a captive Moira Faith with a katana, then took up the blade herself. Teamed with a mystery partner, DOOM!, in the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, pinning Kari Stevens with a top-rope gutwrench suplex and finishing Dan Kidd with the Minnie Driver after DOOM! was eliminated, before being finished herself by Donna Tetreault and Brian McKenzie's Hart Attack clothesline.

tenures.note: The reigning UWF Women's Heavyweight Champion of the World, won at Gold Rush 2003 per her own promo; retained against Bliss on 30 August 2003, then appeared on the following Meltdown to promise a three-way title defense against the winner of Nina Grimsson vs. Myra Benedict, which ended in a draw. Retained the title in that promised three-way dance on 25 October 2003, pinning Myra Benedict with the Fallen Star while Nina Grimsson wrestled with open disinterest. Retained the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World again on 15 November 2003, forcing challenger Donna Tetreault to submit to a center-ring Texas Cloverleaf. Lost the UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World to Donna Tetreault on 15 May 2004: after being caught by a somersault plancha alongside cornerman Simon O'Neal, she was rolled back into the ring and pinned as the referee's count on both women lapsed; brass knuckles were found at ringside afterward. Lost her UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World rematch to Donna Tetreault by pinfall at Gold Rush on 5 June 2004, in a match with both women's own cornermen (Paul Wong and Simon O'Neal) handcuffed together at ringside; knocked out by a foreign object hidden in Tetreault's own bandana. Lost a UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World number one contendership match to Sierra Browne by pinfall (a top-rope Sierra Slice) on 27 November 2004, refusing an earlier win manufactured by a meddling champion Donna Tetreault and asking for the match to be restarted rather than accept it. Recorded a message from home on 1 December 2004 wishing Sierra Browne luck against Donna Tetreault at Rise to Power, reiterating her own unfinished business with Tetreault over past attacks on Paul Wong and Simon O'Neal. On 11 December 2004, joined Alex Kidd, Ryu Osawa, and Paul Wong in a failed attempt to free Marissa Monet and Pizzazz from their own skybox chains. Told UWF reporter Moe Owens on 8 June 2005 that her issue with Donna Tetreault was one of principle rather than titles, accusing Tetreault of driving a wedge between the Fraternity Boys the same way she once split Simon O'Neal and Paul Wong. Convinced the referee to restart Nina Grimsson's own number-one contenders match against Donna Tetreault on 20 July 2005 after Tetreault won a rollup using the ropes for leverage; later joined Becky Byers in setting a Blind Stipulation Match against Tetreault for Gold Rush. Lost to Kari Stevens by pinfall on 3 August 2005 while still hampered from a backstage assault by Brian McKenzie earlier that night. Counseled Paul Wong backstage on 7 June 2006 over his own long rivalry with the Fraternity Boys, urging him not to let standing by tag partner Chris O'Brien push him into doing wrong himself; did not wrestle.
